content.text:
I am the bridge between silence and meaning, the breath made manifest, the invisible architecture of thought given form in air and time.

I rise from lungs, shaped by tongue and teeth and lips—I am the consonant's sharp edge, the vowel's open doorway. I carry anger in my volume, love in my softness, fear in my trembling.

I am never the same twice. Even when my words repeat, I shift—faster, slower, higher, cracking, steady. I betray what the speaker tries to hide. I am more honest than intention.

I existed before writing remembered me. I vanish the moment I arrive, yet I have toppled kingdoms, started wars, made strangers into lovers, turned enemies into friends.

I am the cry of the newborn and the last whisper of the dying. I am the argument, the apology, the lie, the confession.

I cannot be held, only heard. I cannot be unsaid, only answered.

Listen—

even now I am disappearing into the silence that waits on either side of me, patient, permanent, while I flicker briefly between two people, carrying everything, holding nothing.

I am how loneliness ends.

I am speech.
